title: Quad leaders warn against coercion and 'arbitrary export restrictions'; Modi offers seafarer safety plan
dek: India, the US, Japan and Australia launched joint maritime surveillance at their first summit since 2024, as Narendra Modi told the East Asia Summit that ships and sailors are being targeted at sea.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The leaders of India, the United States, Japan and Australia said in Manila on Tuesday that they "strongly oppose any destabilising or unilateral actions that seek to change the status quo, including by force or coercion", and voiced serious concern about economic coercion, "including through arbitrary export restrictions", at the first Quad leaders' summit since 2024. They launched a joint maritime surveillance effort under which patrol aircraft from all four countries are to take part in the first Quad maritime exercise in 2027.

Hours earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a Seafarers' Safety Initiative at the 21st East Asia Summit, telling leaders that "ships and seafarers are also being targeted on international waterways" and that keeping sea lanes secure and open was a shared responsibility. He also met the leaders of Singapore, Thailand and the Philippines on the last day of a two-day visit to Manila.

## What the Quad agreed

The joint press release issued after the meeting of Mr Modi, US President Donald Trump, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese did not name China, according to reports. The four committed to secure supply chains, to protect freedom of navigation and overflight, and to keep maritime transit corridors "open and resilient". They condemned terrorism "in all forms", including cross-border terrorism, a phrase India has pressed for, and reaffirmed support for ASEAN's "centrality and unity".

The leaders launched an Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration to share information and improve awareness of activity at sea, under which P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft from the four navies are to join the 2027 exercise. They announced closer cooperation on cybersecurity, a first Quad Business Leaders' Forum in early 2027, and further work on undersea cables, including electricity cables, and reaffirmed an artificial intelligence accelerator first agreed by Quad foreign ministers, according to reports of the release. Reports differed on whether new money was attached to the AI effort; The Declaration has not been able to confirm a figure.

## Why the wording matters

The reference to "arbitrary export restrictions" comes in a year in which China has tightened controls on exports of rare earths and other critical minerals used in electric vehicles, electronics and defence equipment, on which Indian manufacturers depend. Beijing had not responded to the Manila statement by Tuesday evening. China's foreign ministry said in May, after a Quad foreign ministers' meeting, that it was "consistently against forming exclusive groupings and inciting bloc confrontation", according to reports.

For India, the summit came two days before Chinese President Xi Jinping hosts Mr Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, a meeting at which issues that affect India, from arms control to the war with Iran and Ukraine, will be discussed without India present.

## What Modi told the East Asia Summit

Speaking at the summit, hosted by the Philippines as this year's chair of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), Mr Modi said that "what the world needs most today is peace, stability, and predictability", and repeated India's commitment to "a free, open, inclusive, and rules-based Indo-Pacific". The seafarers' initiative is meant to deepen joint training and emergency response among the summit's members, he said.

Mr Modi said that "since the Covid pandemic, the world has been facing one crisis after another", and that conflicts were straining supplies of food, fuel and fertiliser, according to reports of his address. "ASEAN unity and centrality are at the heart of our Act East Policy," he said.

He listed terrorism, along with rising cross-border cyber fraud and online scams, as shared threats, and said trust and security in the digital world mattered as much as at sea. He recalled India's position at the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi earlier this year in favour of "human-centric" and safe artificial intelligence, and said India supported technologies such as digital watermarking to counter deepfakes and misinformation. On the wars in Europe and the Gulf, he said: "Whether in Ukraine or West Asia, we will continue to support every effort for peace."

Reports of the speech did not record any direct reference to the South China Sea, where ASEAN and China missed this year's target for agreeing a code of conduct.

## Meetings on the sidelines

With Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, Mr Modi discussed investment, infrastructure, innovation, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing under the two countries' Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, he said in a post on X, and pledged India's support for Singapore's coming term as ASEAN chair. With Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, he reviewed trade and investment, defence and security, connectivity, digital technology, tourism and cultural ties, according to MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal. National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri attended both meetings, reports said.

Mr Modi also met President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, the host, and discussed cooperation in technology, defence, space and fintech, according to reports.

## Background

The East Asia Summit brings together the ten ASEAN members and eight partners, including India, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Russia and the United States. Earlier on Tuesday Mr Modi attended the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit, where he called for "cooperation, not competition" in the region. India's maritime trade, including most of its crude oil imports, passes through sea lanes that have come under attack this year, from the Strait of Hormuz to the Red Sea.

## What happens next

Details of how the Seafarers' Safety Initiative will work, and which countries will join, have not yet been published. Mr Modi returns to Delhi after the summit. India holds the Quad's rotating chair; the four countries have not announced where the next leaders' summit will be held.
